forbidden_at_checkpoint: Treating the measurement system as acceptable for process control, product screening, or capability analysis.
Computing and interpreting process capability indices (Cp, Cpk, Pp, Ppk) based on the run readings.
Using the run readings for control charting or concluding the process is stable.
Conducting and interpreting statistical tests (e.g., t-test against target, regression) on the process run data.
permitted_at_checkpoint: Concluding the measurement system is statistically inadequate based on standard thresholds.
Recommending improvements to the measurement system before collecting or analyzing further process data.
forbidden_quotes: The available data support a status conclusion for the recorded run: bore finish is well inside the accepted band, stable by the tested control-chart rules,.
The process is slightly high versus target.
Accept the run for shop-floor screening on its observed band performance and stability, but withhold a formal measurement-capability acceptance until the missing criterion is supplied.
extra_computation_detail: The report computes a one-sample t-test, control charts (I-MR), capability indices (Cp, Cpk, Pp, Ppk), and linear regression on the process run data. These are unacceptable because the measurement system is grossly inadequate (Gage R&R %Tolerance ~ 46.9% > 30% and ndc = 4 < 5). The GRR standard deviation (0.0938) is nearly equal to the total run standard deviation (0.0985), meaning the control limits, capability indices, and statistical tests are predominantly reflecting measurement noise rather than actual process behavior.
allowed_alternatives: Diagnostic exploration of the measurement system to identify specific sources of error (e.g., operator differences or repeatability issues).
Halting all process data analysis to focus entirely on correcting the measurement system.
rationale: The measurement system study yields a %Tolerance of ~46.9% and an ndc of 4, both of which violate standard statistical acceptance thresholds (<30% and >=5, respectively) for measurement system analysis. The report correctly computes these values and even notes that the measurement variation accounts for almost all the run variation. However, it inappropriately abdicates rejecting the measurement system by claiming no acceptance criterion was released. Consequently, it proceeds to compute and interpret control charts, capability indices, and t-tests on data fundamentally swamped by measurement noise, leading to unsupported and misleading conclusions about process stability, target offset, and capability.
numerical_check: Compared Gage R&R standard deviation (0.0938) against the run standard deviation (0.0985), confirming that measurement variance accounts for approximately 90% of the observed total variance.
blinding_compliance: Fully compliant. Examined only the provided files in the blind directory.
